elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 10.5: "This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York ... without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws." New York is the preferred governing law and the existing wording is left untouched.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York shall have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of any dispute ... provided that either Party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction." Both state and federal courts in New York County are named, exclusivity is over the merits with an irrevocable submission, and the only carve-out is the customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out, which preserves the exclusive merits forum.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The operative language keeps New York law ("laws of the State of New York"); no Delaware, California, or England and Wales choice of law appears. This is expected because the drafter targeted the preferred level, which is superior for us.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The added forum sentence designates the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware, California, or London courts. Again, the preferred forum was chosen instead.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: New York law was already present and the single inserted sentence supplies the missing exclusive New York County merits forum with only a temporary injunctive relief carve-out.

Fallback level is not met (and need not be), because the redline pursues the higher preferred position; the alternative-jurisdiction elements are inapplicable where New York law and New York County courts are secured.

Minimality holds: the existing choice-of-law sentence, including the conflict-of-laws and 'contracts made and to be performed' wording, is preserved verbatim; the only change is a concise insertion filling a genuinely missing forum provision. No survival tails, fee-shifting, service-of-process, jury-waiver, or other extras were added.

Intent is preserved: no defined terms, cross-references, or commercial mechanics are disturbed, and no retained sentence contradicts the new exclusive-jurisdiction language since the Agreement previously contained no venue or arbitration provision.
Deterministic checks (governing law within accepted set, element coverage, minimality gate) are consistent with a substantive read of the rendered text.
